open.summary: Uncached searches are slow: index-units search took 9.2 s on first run versus 0.19 s on repeat, with the same plan
open.detail: Read-only live evidence 2026-10-21 (docs/audit/2026-10-21-database-performance-evidence.md): the first run read 8,413 blocks (about 66 MB) from outside the 256 MB Postgres buffer cache at roughly 1 ms each; the repeat read none. Database 8.8 GB. The term-overlap branch pulled 6,568 units (3,389 kept) for a three-word query, then fetched each embedding and search_tsv. Over 34 days, only 22 to 55 percent of TOAST page requests on the search tables (embeddings and long text) were served from the buffer cache, versus 99.9 percent for documents. NOT YET PROVEN: how often real searches are uncached, or that more memory fixes it (effective_cache_size is only a planner estimate; two back-to-back runs are not a controlled test). NEXT: read the Supabase dashboard memory and cache-hit charts and repeat the capture after a known idle gap. THEN OWNER DECISION: (a) larger compute size, paid, dashboard only; or (b) bound the term-overlap branch before ranking, a RAG behaviour change needing a live canary pair.
